issue.title: Task-wikilink cold index runs an unchunked ~20-28 ms basename rebuild after its last yield
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-kj.6 (note #2, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP) and triaged by the bob-cli-kj
land agent. kj.6 measured it while fixing bob-cli-f8 and found it independent of the
decorateRow/hidden-class cause it repaired. It is not caused by bob-cli-kj.

## What is wrong

`TaskWikilinkIndex.warmUpFromVault` (bob-plugins
`plugins/block-id-prompt/src/036-task-wikilink-index.js`, ~lines 440-515) ingests notes
in scheduled chunks and yields once a chunk passes `yieldAfterMs`, under the 16 ms
cold-build chunk contract. After the last yield, though, the `finally { this.endBatch() }`
runs `rebuildBasename()` (`buildBasenameIndex([...this.entries.keys()])`, ~line 115)
synchronously over every entry, together with any files ingested since that yield.

kj.6's developer diagnostic (`scripts/task-wikilink-index-perf-diag.cjs`, which now
reports `tailCpuMs`) measured this un-yielded tail at **15.7-27.8 ms of CPU** on the
6,500-note / 5,000-task synthetic vault. Scheduled chunks stayed under 16 ms. The
performance test (`scripts/test-block-id-prompt-task-wikilink-index-performance.cjs`)
samples only scheduled chunks (`chunkCpuMs`), so the tail never counts against the
16 ms budget.

## Impact

On a cold `((` picker index build, Obsidian's main thread runs one ~20-28 ms block
right at the end of warm-up. That can drop a frame or two during typing just after a
vault opens. It is a one-time jank, not a steady-state cost.

## Fix direction

Keep the 16 ms scheduled-chunk contract. Either chunk the final basename rebuild (or
build it incrementally while ingesting, so `endBatch` only finalizes), or yield before
`endBatch` and rebuild in bounded slices. Then make the performance test charge the
tail against the chunk budget so it cannot regress silently. Do not raise the 16 ms
budget.
